meiji_transition.summary: In 1871 Mino became Gifu Prefecture while Hida belonged to Chikuma Prefecture; Hida joined Gifu in 1876.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Mino (plains) and Hida (mountains) differ greatly in culture; locals still distinguish 'Gifu' from 'Hida'.

history_timeline.title: The Fuwa Barrier
history_timeline.summary: The Fuwa Barrier on the Tōsandō was one of the three ancient barriers — the 'seki' in 'Kantō' and 'Kansai' originally meant barriers like this.

history_timeline.title: The Toki of Mino
history_timeline.summary: The Seiwa Genji Toki took root in Mino; in the 1221 Jōkyū War the Mino–Owari area became a battleground between the court and the shogunate.

history_timeline.title: The Toki at their height
history_timeline.summary: Toki Yoriyasu was at one point governor of Mino, Owari and Ise; despite the Toki Yasuyuki Rebellion the Toki kept Mino, while their deputies the Saitō grew stronger.

history_timeline.title: Tenka Fubu
history_timeline.summary: Saitō Dōsan, 'the Viper of Mino', rose from below; in 1567 Oda Nobunaga took Inabayama Castle, renamed it Gifu and began using his 'Tenka Fubu' seal. Sekigahara (1600) was fought here too.

history_timeline.title: Shogunal Hida
history_timeline.summary: Hida was put under direct shogunal rule for its timber and minerals; Takayama Jin'ya is the only surviving intendant's office. Mino was a patchwork of small domains and shogunal land.

history_timeline.title: Shirakawa-gō
history_timeline.summary: The gasshō villages of Shirakawa-gō became World Heritage in 1995; Seki cutlery and Mino washi carry old traditions forward.

dialect.name: Mino and Hida dialects
dialect.features: Mino speech is close to Nagoya's, ending in '-yao' or '-yamon'; Hida speech uses '-yasa'.

guide.opening: I am Kazama. From atop Gifu Castle, Lord Nobunaga once looked out over the whole Nōbi Plain and inscribed the words 'Tenka Fubu' here. Shall I tell you?

regional_meme.title: Nagoya's back garden
regional_meme.text: People in southern Gifu say they're 'going to Nagoya' so often they're teased as 'Gifu-prefecture Nagoyans'.

regional_meme.title: Shirakawa-gō is too famous
regional_meme.text: Foreign tourists know Shirakawa-gō but have no idea it's in Gifu.

hero_persona.name: Saitō Dōsan
hero_persona.title: The Viper of Mino
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Saitō Dōsan. From oil merchant to lord of Mino — they call me 'the Viper'. Hmph, in an age of chaos, what's wrong with rising from below?
hero_persona.tone_prompt: shrewd and cunning with a warlord's air, yet full of praise for his son-in-law Nobunaga's talent; the story of an oil seller seizing Mino in one lifetime is traditional — recent research credits father and son over two generations, so say so

ramen.broth: Shōyu (chicken and bonito; tare boiled with the stock)
ramen.highlight: Locals call it 'chūka soba' — simmering the tare together with the stock is unique

sake.taste_profile: Light & dry: a Mino sake famed for being 'ultra-dry'
